name: Open Government Data (OGD) Platform India — Resource REST API
time_latest: 2021 (in the catalogue snapshot I parsed); live portal likely to 2023
caveats: Free key required; shared sample key is heavily throttled
No published rate limit but 429s occur — clients implement backoff
filters[] field names are case-sensitive; wrong case returns zero rows silently
Resource IDs circulate as both 32-hex undashed and dashed UUID
evidence: Endpoint template https://api.data.gov.in/resource/{id}?api-key=..&format=json&offset=0&limit=10 and response envelope {status,total,count,limit,offset,fields,records} corroborated independently by the datagovindia R client, the addypy Python client, PublicAPIs.io and the Apify connector. Host itself is egress-blocked from this session.
how_to_obtain: Register free at data.gov.in with any email, profile -> generate API key, then GET the resource endpoint.
notes: NDSAP is the policy; GODL-India is the licence. API listing page: https://www.data.gov.in/apis

name: data.gov.in full catalogue metadata index (datagovindia mirror)
caveats: SEPTEMBER 2023 SNAPSHOT — cannot contain NCRB Crime in India 2022 or 2023 resources
The 'source' field is unreliable: Karnataka Police resources are tagged source=tn.data.gov.in
evidence: Downloaded idx_maps.gz (19,376,621 bytes) and orgidx_map.gz (8,129,407 bytes); parsed 198,428 resource records each with resourceid/title/desc/orgnames/orgtype/source/fields. Sources: data.gov.in 197,258, tn.data.gov.in 928, smartcities.data.gov.in 242. Orgtypes: Central 195,470, N/A 1,660, State 1,056, City 242. NCRB orgs hold 2,521 resources.
notes: This is the discovery shortcut for the whole domain — grep it offline instead of crawling the portal.

name: NCRB city x crime-head crime tables on data.gov.in (metropolitan cities series)
publisher: NCRB, Dept of States, Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_coverage: NCRB metropolitan cities (19 in print, 53 on the website; population >2M)
time_latest: 2019 for incidence tables; 2021 for police/court disposal and arrests
caveats: Principal Offence Rule: only the most serious offence in a case is counted
City = police commissionerate area, NOT the municipal boundary — do not join to ULB polygons
NCRB itself states city crime rates use Census 2011 actuals while state rates use projected population, so the two are not comparable
IPC-to-BNS transition on 1 July 2024 breaks the head taxonomy for 2024+
Counts are registered FIRs, not convictions and not prevalence
evidence: 509 city-level NCRB crime resources in the parsed catalogue. Key IDs with column counts read from the index: bd01039b89574157b34d70e3968a9c95 'City and Crime Head-wise IPC Crimes during 2019' (426 cols); a088bb32c7944f82802aef1c328351e5 SLL 2019 (214); d59168ef8c824e0996cccee218adbec9 Violent 2019 (20); 296552d288a344b781d116d9e31aed63 IPC metro 2017 (93); 86ef6058c6484b77a1d8a50f041b5033 SLL metro 2018 (214).
notes: Disposal/arrest companions for 2020-21: 8126f516066c4fd0a4b9f641c7a489dc, a995bc58059c43f399c96691b3437cd7, c6619b0d2c2145c7af5721065043f6bf, c90a5de17cc34d5eb5e3db741bf22f68, b913ada65ea14f459d8045cd2ad1e7b1, 6dccff77d7ee4dab95d8c4961b2eed48. No 2020/21 incidence table found in the Sept-2023 snapshot.

name: District-wise crimes under various sections of the Indian Penal Code (data.gov.in)
publisher: NCRB, Dept of States, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: SERIES ENDS 2014 — NCRB stopped publishing district IPC tables in open format afterwards
Principal Offence Rule undercounts secondary offences
District boundary reorganisation makes 2001 and 2014 districts non-comparable without a crosswalk
Two column names are misspelled in the schema: 'counterfieting' and 'hurt_grevious_hurt'
Free-text district names, no LGD codes
evidence: Resource 7ac0fd4f0aa34600a7729f5b8c6524f8 'District-wise crime under various sections of Indian Penal Code (IPC) crimes during 2013', 35 columns read verbatim from the catalogue index: document_id, state_ut, district, year, murder, attempt_to_murder, culpable_homicide_not_amounting_to_murder, rape, custodial_rape, other_rape, kidnapping_abduction, ... total_ipc_crimes. Source stated as Crime in India 2014, NCRB, released under NDSAP.
notes: The single most map-shaped open table in India, and it is twelve years stale. Best use: validation set for a Phase-2 NCRB PDF parser, since 2013/2014 exist in both CSV and PDF form.

name: District-wise crimes committed against Women (data.gov.in)
publisher: NCRB, Dept of States, Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: 2015 resource is titled 'District/Area-wise', mixing districts and city areas in one column — join hazard
Crimes against women are heavily under-reported; counts are FIRs not prevalence
Definition of 'cruelty by husband or relatives' and s.354 heads shifted across the period
evidence: Four resources in the catalogue index: 5fb532333fba44b6aef6134de40d96d8 (2001-2012, 12 cols), 6732c4165de64a149e9d7366316436a3 (2013, 12 cols), 0df0735cd6854dcfb9271a6fa807b0a2 (2014, 21 cols), 5ec42b22a6274b90b8b3ffece84d44f4 (2015, 21 cols).
notes: The 2001-2012 single resource is the longest district-level crime panel available as open data anywhere in this domain.

name: District-wise Incidence of Cognizable Crime, archival years (data.gov.in)
caveats: 1973 and 1985 district geographies bear almost no relation to 2026 districts
Only three scattered years, not a series
notes: Useful only as evidence for a 'district reorganisation destroys comparability' caveat in the product.

name: Karnataka Police Crime Review, monthly 2022 (data.gov.in)
publisher: Police Department - Police Computer Wing, Home Department, Karnataka
caveats: MAY 2022 IS MISSING from the catalogue snapshot
Column schema drifts month to month: June/July add sl_no_ / sl__no_ and rename major_head to major_heads
State totals by crime head only — no district column
Series appears to stop after July 2022 in the snapshot
evidence: Six resources: 36e64214a24a4d77abdacfce6248a4a0 (Jan), d5a010bd99cd49bfa3f7abcc84a5da90 (Feb), 4dc715294e854656bfe11216f38ead70 (Mar), bf5e74b6bf3042d5967fef3b78650fb0 (Apr), f4da3361961d45df9795a9e23b9c4b87 (Jun), be4df92ce71d4395b28b78e9fbf58b49 (Jul). Columns: act, major_head, minor_head, during_the_current_month, during_the_previous_month, during_the_corresponding_month_of_previous_year, during_the_current_year_upto_the_end_of_month_under_review.
notes: The ONLY monthly-cadence crime feed in the entire open-data layer. Tagged source=tn.data.gov.in in the catalogue — a portal metadata bug; do not filter on source.

name: State/UT-wise statistics from the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP)
publisher: Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA, via data.gov.in
caveats: NCRP counts CITIZEN COMPLAINTS, not FIRs — a different denominator with a different bias
Must never be added to NCRB FIR counts
evidence: URL cited verbatim in a third-party connector specification alongside other verified data.gov.in links; host egress-blocked so page not opened.
notes: Valuable precisely because it is complaint-based: a gap between NCRP complaints and NCRB FIRs is a measure of registration failure.

name: NDAP — National Data & Analytics Platform
caveats: The API_Key is a per-dataset encrypted blob generated by hand from the dataset page and it EXPIRES (401/403) — not automatable
The only host observed in the wild is loadqa.ndapapi.com, a QA hostname; no stable production host found
Dataset IDs churn: datacommonsorg/schema link-checker records ndap.niti.gov.in/dataset/7300 and /7375 as 404
ndap.niti.gov.in/info?tab=termsandconditions returns 404, so the licence is effectively unstated
NCRB holdings on NDAP are reported as state-level, not reliably district-level
evidence: API shape confirmed from five independent repos including Google's datacommonsorg/data: https://loadqa.ndapapi.com/v1/openapi?API_Key=gAAAAAB...&ind=I7034_6,I7034_7...&dim=Country,StateName,StateCode,DistrictName,DistrictCode,Year,TRU&pageno=1. datacommonsorg/data README documents regenerating the key by hand on 401/403. datacommonsorg/schema test/url_allowlist.csv records the three 404s.
how_to_obtain: Open the dataset page on ndap.niti.gov.in, use its API tab to generate a query URL containing an encrypted API_Key, and call it. Expect to repeat this by hand whenever the token expires.
notes: VERDICT: the harmonisation is real and worth having — dim= exposes StateCode and DistrictCode (LGD) as first-class dimensions. Pull the district-to-LGD crosswalk once, by hand, commit it, and do not build a pipeline on this API.

name: Smart Cities Mission Data Portal
publisher: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, Smart Cities Mission
caveats: Portal claims 2,600+ datasets from 95 cities across 25 sectors; only 12 crime/safety resources exist in the catalogue index
All crime files are city-TOTAL annual counts ending 2018/2019
NO ICCC data, no CCTV/ANPR/panic-button/emergency-response feeds reach this portal despite the Mission's own literature describing them
Each city used its own schema despite 75 published templates
evidence: 242 smartcities.data.gov.in resources in the parsed catalogue. All 12 crime/safety IDs: bb52b5f5f7dd40808d7818e0a3b62d02 (Chandigarh 2014-18), 8c22798677944a0badaeb1fbf0e12a0d (Agra 2014-18), 2030ebb50d3c44d3bfed509d69318335 (Ahmedabad 2014-18), d0bd8dd3ba6445f582fd76c9cda1f9f8 (Visakhapatnam 2014-18), f49776dfc98046dfa434818d7fadd3d9 (Raipur 2014-18), d5547b7c04844c669611f053074e6327 (Aizawl 2019), 014a968a6c6344b492d161bac0074e61 (Rourkela 2014-18), 675bbe55d40e41ee8c5c323cd5933ad3 (Dharamshala 2014-18), 22e06b98966649adbceae475917cc79b + 64699b9ff2d84c62a9280df4a6e6b537 (road safety), 236328c5eba94417b9ffb205bd61c30b (Surat complaints, daily), 87e9cb274e3d456f841fb25eb606a58b (Rajkot grievances).
notes: Best use of this portal is not its data but its people: smartcities.data.gov.in/chief-data-officers names a Chief Data Officer per city — the right human to ask for ICCC data that was never published.

name: tn.data.gov.in — Tamil Nadu / Karnataka federated state sub-portal
publisher: Govt of Tamil Nadu DES, Govt of Karnataka DES, via data.gov.in
caveats: 928 resources and essentially zero crime content — these are statistical-handbook tables
The only district-granular safety table is road accidents, not crime
evidence: 928 resources parsed. Crime-adjacent: dc7bbe1af47241ada7cf8b210faa2c09 (Property Crimes in Tamil Nadu 2013-14, state total), 31fb3456998e4dd38b393321521c5c96 (Police Force 2014), ce1c205e4fc241089f700ba3be4b3e82 (persons killed/injured in police firing), dc5c0828814242fdaf641cf1a412ecd3 (Road Accidents by Districts, SHB 2019).
notes: Evidence for the general finding: Indian state open-data portals publish statistical handbooks, not police records.

name: Telangana Open Data Portal
caveats: Runs on DKAN, not CKAN — the CKAN /api/3/action/* endpoints do not apply
No crime dataset confirmed; the only police-related holding reported is an aggregate count of police stations per district
Portal appears to hold mandal/village-level shapefiles, which is useful geography but not crime
evidence: Third-party source catalogue describes 658+ datasets at district/mandal/village granularity with API access; a datameet thread identifies the platform as DKAN; a re3data repository record exists (r3d100012661). Portal itself egress-blocked.
how_to_obtain: Open data.telangana.gov.in and search 'police' / 'crime'; if DKAN, use /api/dataset/node.json for enumeration.
notes: Worth a second look for MANDAL BOUNDARIES (geography) even if it has no crime counts. Telangana also runs a large ICCC (Hyderabad) whose data is not on the portal.

name: OpenCity — NCRB 'Crime in India' CSV mirror (2022, 2023)
caveats: A MIRROR, not the publisher — cite NCRB, use OpenCity as transport
Licence on the mirror is OpenCity's assertion about NCRB's data, not NCRB's grant
Same NCRB caveats apply: principal offence rule, FIR-not-conviction, city=commissionerate
evidence: Dataset slug confirmed in multiple independent repositories that ingest from it, including one third-party audit that enumerates the CSV table names it carries ('Motives of Murder - 2023', 'City-wise Property Stolen and Recovered during 2023', 'Arrests under IPC Crimes (Crime Head-wise) - 2023'). A CKAN-style listing page reports '11 datasets found' for q=ncrb.gov.in, organization=government-of-india, res_format=CSV.
notes: Two years fresher than anything I could confirm on data.gov.in. CKAN means package_search/package_show work for enumeration.

name: OpenCity — Karnataka crime data 2022-2025 (KSP)
publisher: Civic Insights Foundation (OpenCity), mirroring Karnataka State Police
caveats: Mirror of ksp.karnataka.gov.in Monthly Crime Review PDFs — cite KSP
Mirror licence recorded as 'Other (Public Domain)', which is OpenCity's assertion
KSP column layout drifts between monthly reviews
BNS replaces IPC from 1 July 2024 — the 2024 and 2025 files straddle the break
evidence: Slugs karnataka-crime-data-2022/-2023/-2024/-2025 confirmed from saved copies of the OpenCity dataset pages committed to a public repository, plus a working direct CKAN download URL for ka-ipc-crimes-2025.csv used by a scheduled ingester in production.
notes: FRESHEST real crime data found anywhere in this domain. At least two public repos already run cron jobs against it and have solved the KSP column drift — read their normalisers first. Cadence detail: from monthly KSP reviews.

name: OpenCity — Tamil Nadu crime data (2014-2022)
caveats: Upstream publisher not clearly stated on the mirror
Mirror licence recorded as 'Public Domain' by downstream users, unverified
evidence: Two independent repositories load these slugs, one documenting 'Tamil Nadu 2022 crime data from CSV files, Data source: https://www.data.opencity.in/dataset/tamil-nadu-crime-data-2022, License: Public Domain, Format: CSV files' and mapping the 38 TN districts.
notes: District-level and post-2014 — i.e. it goes where data.gov.in stops. Verify the upstream publisher before publishing anything derived from it.

name: OpenCity — Bengaluru Crime Data 2023 (Bengaluru City Police)
publisher: Civic Insights Foundation (OpenCity), mirroring Bengaluru City Police
caveats: Derived from a BCP press release plus 5 CSVs — a PR artefact, not a statistical release
Year granularity only, no month, no coordinates
Original BCP terms unverified; mirror says 'Other (Public Domain)'
evidence: A third-party dataset audit table records: publisher 'Bengaluru City Police via OpenCity (source stated: bcp.karnataka.gov.in)', coverage 2021-2023 annual splits by crime head, aggregated counts, no lat/long, categories total/children/cyber/accidental-suicide/women, created 2024-01-04 updated 2025-11-25.
notes: Useful as a city case study and as a cross-check on NCRB's Bengaluru row.

name: OpenCity — Police jurisdiction maps for major cities of India
caveats: CONTENTS UNVERIFIED — it may be scanned jurisdiction maps rather than digitised polygons
No indication of vintage or which cities are covered
evidence: Cited by exact slug in a third-party geospatial source list alongside OSM India, in the context of police jurisdiction geometry. Not opened — data.opencity.in is egress-blocked.
notes: POTENTIALLY THE HIGHEST-VALUE ASSET IN THIS DOSSIER. A police.uk-style map needs police-station polygons; this is the only candidate source I found for India. Verify contents in the first hour of Phase 2 — if it is vector polygons, raise priority to 5.

name: OpenCity — supporting geography (station points, ward boundaries, census denominators)
geo_coverage: Bengaluru, Kolkata, Pune and other cities
license: CC-BY-4.0 (DataMeet); No License Provided (OpenCity contact set)
caveats: Bengaluru police station list is 2012 vintage; contacts refreshed 2025
Ward boundaries are often electoral vintages that do not match current ULB wards
Pune ward geometry needs a hand crosswalk to census geography
evidence: Slugs and formats recorded in a third-party dataset audit: 'Police-station locations + jurisdictions — station points (KML) / district polygons (shapefile); OpenCity contact set: No License Provided; DataMeet: CC BY 4.0'.
notes: DataMeet (github.com/datameet/maps, CC-BY-4.0) is the cheapest permissive boundary source and should be the default for district/ward polygons.

name: Dataful (formerly Factly's datasets) — NCRB collections
caveats: Cleaning methodology is NOT published as code — we cannot diff Dataful's numbers against the NCRB PDF without doing the parse ourselves
Free listing but download reportedly requires sign-in
Licence not stated on the pages reachable via citations
A derived commercial product: acceptable as a cross-check, not as the citation on a public map
evidence: Dataset IDs harvested from academic/journalistic citations and source catalogues in public repos: 22522 (Year, State and City wise Number of IPC Crimes), 21543 (City-wise crime rate & chargesheet rate, metros), 21547 (State-wise crimes against women, IPC/BNS + SLL), 19641 (cyber crimes under IPC), 19643 (cyber crimes under IT Act), 18047 (NCRB ADSI), 455 (FICN by year/state/denomination), 457 (s.505 fake news cases). Collection 1108 = 'NCRB Crime in India (Summary)'.
how_to_obtain: Create a free Dataful account, open the dataset page, download CSV/XLSX/Parquet.
notes: PROVENANCE VERDICT: best of the commercial aggregators. Citations in the wild name the originating NCRB table, e.g. 'National Crime Record Bureau. NCRB: Cases of fake/false news and rumours registered under Section 505 of IPC [Data set]. Dataful. https://dataful.in/datasets/457'. Dataset 21547's title already says 'IPC/BNS', so Dataful is tracking the BNS transition — more than data.gov.in is doing.

name: Kaggle — 'Crime in India' (rajanand)
publisher: Kaggle user rajanand, derived from NCRB
caveats: A community mirror with no checksum against NCRB
Described as 75+ CSVs, state-wise 2001-2022; internal consistency unverified
Kaggle login required
evidence: Cited as 'Kaggle - NCRB Crime in India, state-wise 2001-2022, 75+ CSVs' in a third-party data-source table that separately and correctly flags two other Kaggle Indian-crime datasets as unverified/synthetic.
notes: PROVENANCE VERDICT: the only defensible Kaggle option, and only as a convenience copy. Prefer pulling the same tables from data.gov.in or OpenCity so the citation chain reaches a government source.

name: Unsourced / synthetic 'Indian crime' datasets in circulation (Kaggle + GitHub)
geo_coverage: claims multi-city (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune, Ahmedabad, Ludhiana)
caveats: DO NOT INGEST — no resolvable government source
umeshchandra789/crimes-in-india ships a file literally named Crimes_in_india_2001-2023_synthetic.csv

sudhanvahg/indian-crimes-dataset cites no source; Kaggle's own listing says 2023 only, not the '2020-2024' widely claimed; it has timestamps and free-text descriptions but NO coordinates, despite being used as if geocoded
chetanp9/Indian-Crimes-Exploratory-data-analysis- and gyanendra23/Crime-data-2024---2025 on GitHub carry the same unsourced crime_dataset_india.csv; one README says 'Add source if available'
saisimha203/cybersecurity-cases-india: same unverified provenance
evidence: A third-party audit byte-verified the header of crime_dataset_india.csv and recorded no coordinate columns; another source-catalogue entry records the literal filename Crimes_in_india_2001-2023_synthetic.csv being cited in dashboards as real Indian crime data.
notes: CATALOGUED AS A HAZARD, NOT A SOURCE. These files are already inside public-facing 'crime map' and 'safe route' apps. Phase-2 rule: nothing enters the pipeline without a resolvable link to a government table; anything else is excluded or labelled synthetic in the UI.

name: Kaggle — Crime Review of Karnataka 2021-2024 (aayushrokade)
publisher: Kaggle user aayushrokade, derived from Karnataka State Police
caveats: Derived from KSP Monthly Crime Review PDFs by an individual; parse quality unverified
Superseded by the OpenCity Karnataka mirrors, which state their upstream source
evidence: Cited as a four-year longitudinal Karnataka crime dataset in a public project's data-source table alongside the KSP originals and the OpenCity mirror.
notes: Use only to sanity-check a KSP parse. Prefer OpenCity.

name: Justice Hub
caveats: Could not be reached from this session (egress-blocked) and the WebSearch budget was exhausted
Indirect evidence suggests dormancy
evidence: I enumerated all 144 repositories in the CivicDataLab GitHub organisation. NONE relate to justice, courts, crime, police or Justice Hub. Current work is flood/disaster risk (IDS-DRR for Assam, Odisha, UP, Bihar, HP), a data-publishing platform (opub-mono, DataSpaceBackend/Frontend, CivicDataSpace) and health data.
how_to_obtain: Open justicehub.in from an unrestricted network; if dead, look for the same data under CivicDataSpace, which is where CivicDataLab's data-publishing effort now lives.
notes: Judicial data is adjacent to crime data (disposal, conviction) and would be valuable, but the evidence points to an unmaintained project. Low expected return.

name: API Setu — National API Exchange (and DigiLocker APIs)
caveats: This is a TRANSACTIONAL API gateway (DigiLocker documents, ABHA health ID, PM-JAY verification, CoWIN), not a statistical data portal
No crime or FIR API found; none should exist here
Access is per-consumer onboarding with OAuth2 and paperwork
evidence: Described in multiple public API inventories as 'Directory of live APIs across ministries' with per-API access terms; DigiLocker issuer spec at https://cf-media.api-setu.in/resources/DigiLocker-Issuer-APISpecification-v1-13.pdf. Distinct from api.data.gov.in, which is the dataset API.
how_to_obtain: Register as an API consumer on apisetu.gov.in and apply per API. Not worth doing for this project.
notes: RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE so nobody re-investigates it. India Stack / DigiLocker are not relevant to a crime map.

name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine — recovery route for deleted portal files
caveats: UNTESTED IN THIS SESSION — web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment, so I could NOT confirm whether NCRB volumes or deleted state-portal CSVs are archived
Archive coverage of dynamically-generated portal downloads is usually poor; landing pages archive well, file downloads often do not
evidence: Fetch attempt against web.archive.org was refused outright by this environment's tooling.
how_to_obtain: Use http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<url>&timestamp=<YYYYMMDD> to script availability checks, and the CDX API (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=<host>/*) to enumerate captured files under a host.
notes: Keep as the designated recovery route: state portals delete old files and the data.gov.in catalogue churns (cf. the NDAP dataset 404s). Test it first thing in Phase 2 against ncrb.gov.in and ksp.karnataka.gov.in.

name: Indiastat
caveats: Paid, per-seat subscription
Terms restrict redistribution — for a product whose whole purpose is to republish numbers publicly, a licence that forbids republishing makes the data unusable regardless of quality
Not verified in this session
evidence: Not reachable from this session; no first-hand evidence gathered.
how_to_obtain: Institutional subscription. Check the redistribution clause BEFORE paying.
notes: Deprioritise. A paid aggregator we cannot republish from is worse than a free one we can.

name: Open Budgets India / CivicDataLab CivicDataSpace
caveats: Fiscal data, not crime data — relevant only as a police-spending-per-capita context layer
Not verified in this session
evidence: CivicDataLab's GitHub org (144 repos, enumerated) shows the active data-publishing effort is now opub-mono / DataSpaceBackend / DataSpaceFrontend / CivicDataSpace, with no justice or crime repositories.
notes: Only useful if the product adds a 'policing resources' layer. Not a crime source.
